title: anomalyco/opencode — The open source coding agent.
content:
The open source AI coding agent.
English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 한국어 | Deutsch | Español | Français | Italiano | Dansk | 日本語 | Polski | Русский | Bosanski | العربية | Norsk | Português (Brasil) | ไทย | Türkçe | Українська | বাংলা | Ελληνικά | Tiếng Việt
# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
# Package managers
npm i -g opencode-ai@latest        # or bun/pnpm/yarn
scoop install opencode             # Windows
choco install opencode             # Windows
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-bin               # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run nixpkgs#opencode           # or github:anomalyco/opencode for latest dev branch
Tip
Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.
OpenCode is also available as a desktop application. Download directly from the releases page or opencode.ai/download.
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
# Windows (Scoop)
scoop bucket add extras; scoop install extras/opencode-desktop
The install script respects the following priority order for the installation path:
- $OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR - Custom installation directory
- $XDG_BIN_DIR - XDG Base Directory Specification compliant path
- $HOME/bin - Standard user binary directory (if it exists or can be created)
- $HOME/.opencode/bin - Default fallback
# Examples
OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
XDG_BIN_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
OpenCode includes two built-in agents you can switch between with the Tab key.
- build - Default, full-access agent for development work
- plan - Read-only agent for analysis and code exploration
  - Denies file edits by default
  - Asks permission before running bash commands
  - Ideal for exploring unfamiliar codebases or planning changes
Also included is a general subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks.
This is used internally and can be invoked using @general in messages.
Learn more about agents.
For more info on how to configure OpenCode, head over to our docs.
If you're interested in contributing to OpenCode, please read our contributing docs before submitting a pull request.
If you are working on a project that's related to OpenCode and is using "opencode" as part of its name, for example "opencode-dashboard" or "opencode-mobile", please add a note to your README to clarify that it is not built by the OpenCode team and is not affiliated with us in any way.

report.summary: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that runs in the terminal, offering build and plan agents for automated development and analysis.
report.background: The rise of AI coding agents has created demand for transparent, self-hosted alternatives to commercial assistants. OpenCode, developed by anomalyco, positions itself as an open-source coding agent that runs directly in the terminal, addressing concerns around vendor lock-in, privacy, and customization. It has expanded beyond a simple CLI by offering a desktop application and comprehensive documentation translated into many languages. The project includes a structured agent system: a full-access 'build' agent for hands-on development and a read-only 'plan' agent for exploration and analysis. This mirrors a broader industry trend where developer tools increasingly separate execution from planning to improve safety and controllability. OpenCode's broad installation support—via npm, Homebrew, Scoop, pacman, Nix, and a curl script—shows a focus on accessibility for developers across platforms. The project also sets community guidelines, including a naming convention for third-party integrations, indicating it expects a growing ecosystem around the core agent.
key_points: OpenCode is an open-source coding agent designed to live in the terminal, giving developers a free and customizable alternative to closed coding assistants. It supports multiple installation methods, including a one-line script, npm, Homebrew, Scoop, and system package managers.

It includes two built-in agent modes: 'build' has full access for development work, while 'plan' is read-only, denies file edits by default, and requests permission before running shell commands. This safety-focused split helps users analyze code without risking unintended changes.

There is also a general subagent used internally for complex searches and multistep tasks. Users can invoke it with @general in messages, enabling more powerful multi-step problem solving within the same interface.

OpenCode is available as a desktop application on macOS and Windows in addition to the CLI, making it approachable for users who prefer graphical tools. Documentation is translated into many languages, broadening its global developer reach.

The project sets clear community guidelines: third-party projects using the name 'opencode' must state they are not affiliated with the official team. This protects the brand while encouraging open collaboration and integration development.
report.impact: For the AI industry, OpenCode demonstrates that coding agents can be open source while offering sophisticated workflow features like plan/build separation and subagents. Developers gain a transparent, locally controllable alternative to proprietary assistants, enabling deeper customization, auditability, and integration with existing toolchains. The plan agent's permission-gated design highlights a shift toward safer agent interactions in day-to-day development. Regular users benefit from easy installs and a desktop option, lowering the barrier to trying AI-assisted programming. As open-source agents mature, they may pressure commercial tools to offer more flexible pricing and privacy options. For teams exploring autonomous coding, OpenCode provides a practical starting point to experiment without losing control over their codebase.
report.tools: If you want to compare or complement OpenCode, watch Aider (terminal pair-programming), OpenHands (autonomous agent platform), Cline (VS Code agent), and Codex CLI from OpenAI. For open-source AI coding ecosystems, Continuum's Continue and Sourcegraph's Cody are also relevant. But first, try OpenCode itself: inspect its repo and use its plan agent to safely explore your own projects.
